title: Frederick Banting's birth chart
metaDescription: Frederick Banting's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 22.1° Scorpio. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Mutable signs carry six of the nine placements whose signs are settled — the broadest certain weighting in the chart. The mutable signs sit where one season is already becoming the next — the scheme’s translators.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 22.1° Scorpio — the third decan, 20°–30°, which the tradition sub-rules by the Moon. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Scorpio and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 2.2° Sagittarius; Venus stands at 6.7° Sagittarius; Mars stands at 15.1° Libra. The tradition reads a mind that decides at speaking speed from Mercury, taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate from Venus, drive that argues its way forward from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Neptune to Pluto is the closest call of the day, a conjunction within 0.1°. When two functions occupy one degree, the tradition reads a fusion: neither can act without committing the other. Behind it, Jupiter square Pluto at 0.2°, and Jupiter square Neptune at 0.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Mercury opposes Neptune while both square Jupiter. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment. The Sun stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has three entries for this chart. Mercury in Sagittarius at 2.2° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Libra at 15.1° is in detriment; Jupiter in Pisces at 8.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 3 water, 3 air, 2 fire, 1 earth by element and 6 mutable, 2 fixed, 1 cardinal by modality. Water weights a chart toward the felt and the remembered — information that arrives as atmosphere before it arrives as words. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Aries into Taurus during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.8° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
